- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day moving avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 10-day moving avg as ceiling.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior range.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply 1.5–3% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is rising.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0% to capture sentiment momentum.
- Avoid forecasting beyond 10-day horizon without sentiment confirmation; if sentiment is volatile, use 7-day moving avg as anchor for 30-day forecast.
